title: Sable and the Verdict
premise: When the coffin of town founder Aldous Verity is opened for the cathedral's sesquicentennial and found empty, archivist Dominic Iversen discovers the exhumation was ordered using forged documents pulled from his own locked archive — documents only a handful of people could have accessed. As Detective Maren Sable investigates, Dominic realizes the killer is someone who has been reading the town's secret files for years, someone who loved the archive as he did. The trail leads to the cathedral's dying canon, who faked his own father's burial fifteen years ago to hide a murder, and to the anniversary dinner where the final file will be read aloud. Dominic must choose between protecting the institution he has served and exposing the truth, ending with him testifying at the canon's bedside trial as the real bones are finally laid to rest — and Maren asks him to help her open the archive to the town at last.
about_author: Elodie Montrose is a former parish records clerk from the Yorkshire coast who spent a decade cataloguing centuries of municipal secrets before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about people who keep other people's secrets, and lives above a decommissioned library with an unreasonably large card catalogue.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On the morning of the founder's ceremonial exhumation, Dominic unlocks the crypt he has tended for fifteen years, only to watch the coffin come up light and hollow. The emotional beat is quiet dread: the one thing he was trusted to protect has failed without him touching it.

chapters.title: A File That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Detective Maren Sable's POV. Maren traces the exhumation order to the cathedral archive and finds a request form bearing Dominic's signature — dated a day he can prove he was in the hospital. She interviews him with professional suspicion; he answers with the precision of a man who has nothing to hide but everything to fear.

chapters.title: Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic audits his own catalogue and finds twelve files subtly altered over the years — dates shifted, pages swapped — a pattern only a devoted reader of the archive could execute. The beat is betrayal: someone has been loving his life's work in order to corrupt it.

chapters.title: The Canon's Confession Booth
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren interviews Canon Aldric Verity, the founder's grandson, now frail and revered. He is gracious, evasive, and quotes archive call numbers from memory. Maren leaves unsettled, aware she is being measured by someone who knows exactly what the records say.

chapters.title: What the Bones Would Say
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A fragment of bone surfaces in the old sexton's garden, and Dominic recognizes the burial ledger entry he once filed as 'corrected.' He begins secretly reconstructing the fifteen-year-old discrepancy between the official death record and the interment record, guilt mounting with each match.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Filed Under V
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren discovers Dominic's private investigation and confronts him: obstruction or ally? Their wary partnership forms over midnight coffee in the archive, and the first thread of trust — and something warmer — is pulled taut between duty and attraction.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. With the sesquicentennial dinner days away, Dominic identifies the three people with archive access across the alteration window: the canon, the sexton, and himself. When the sexton is found dead at the bottom of the crypt stairs, the list shortens and Dominic becomes either the next target or the prime suspect.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren uncovers the buried truth: Aldous Verity died in 1962 by his son's hand, and the canon staged the burial to protect the family name — the 'founder' in the ground was never Aldous at all. The emotional beat is horror at how a whole town's identity was built on a curated file.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Record
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. At the anniversary dinner, the canon plans to read a sanitized founding history and then die quietly, taking the truth with him. Dominic swaps the lectern documents for the true records and publicly reads the murder entry aloud as Maren moves through the crowd; the canon collapses, confessing in front of the town he built.

chapters.title: Open Stacks
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Weeks later, the true remains are reburied with honest words, the canon dies awaiting trial, and Dominic — no longer the keeper of secrets but their witness — unlocks the archive to public researchers for the first time. The final beat is belonging: Maren arrives with a request slip, and he hands her the first file.
